stem_raw:
The surgical hemostatic agents are further divided into the following groups based on the
nature of the agent:
• Caustic agents: They act by causing local tissue destruction, which leads to protein coagulation
and precipitation. This further leads to thrombus formation and sealing of the small blood vessels.
The agents include Monsel solution (a20% ferric nitrate solution), silver nitrate, and aluminum
chloride.
• Biological physical agents: They act by promoting platelet activation and formation of
three-dimensional matrix for the formation of clots. These agents are used in several operations
including neurosurgical, orthopedic, thoracic, abdominal, and vascular procedures. The agents
include gelatin, oxidized cellulose, and microfibrillar collagen.

Solution to Question 11:
The given scenario of recurrent episodes of melena, eczema, and multiple petechiae along with
low platelet counts is suggestive of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome. The diagnostic investigation in this
patient is WASP gene mutation testing. 
Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome(WAS) is an X-linked recessive immunodeficiency disorder. It is caused
by mutations in the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein (WASp) that primarily affects the T
lymphocytes.
Normally, WASp regulates the actin cytoskeleton and thus helps in cell adhesion, migration, and
the formation of synapses between antigen-presenting and target cells. In WAS, there is a
progressive loss of T lymphocytes in the peripheral blood resulting in defects in cellular
immunity. 
The clinical features of WAS are recurrent bacterial infections, eczema, and bleeding due
to thrombocytopenia. Patients with WAS are prone to develop B-cell lymphomas and autoimmune
disorders.

The histopathological image shows the presence of amyloid-rich stroma (pinkish material) and
nests of polygonal cells, which are findings suggestive of medullary carcinoma of thyroid.
Medullary carcinoma of the thyroid (MTC) arises from the parafollicular C cells. Most of the MTC
are sporadic, but they may also be associated with inheritable syndromes like familial
MTC, MEN2A, and MEN2B. All the inherited variants are secondary to RET gene mutations.
Most patients present at 50–60 years and have a female preponderance. MTC secretes calcitonin,
carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA), prostaglandins E2 and F2α, histaminase, serotonin,
and adrenocorticotrophic hormone (ACTH).

Solution to Question 13:
The given clinical history of left flank pain, hematuria, weight loss, headache, nausea, and
convulsions along with the family history of brain tumours and kidney tumours is suggestive of
Von Hippel-Lindau syndrome. (VHL)
VHL syndrome is inherited as an autosomal dominant trait and is characterized by a
predisposition to a variety of neoplasms, particularly hemangioblastomas of the cerebellum and
retina. Hundreds of bilateral renal cysts, often multiple, clear cell carcinomas develop in 40% to
60% of affected persons. Those with VHL syndrome inherit a germline mutation of the VHL gene
on chromosome 3p. A 'second hit' can lead to manifestations as described below.
Other options:
Option A: Li-Fraumeni syndrome is an autosomal dominant disorder due to a defect in the
tumour suppressor gene P53 located on chromosome 17. It is characterised by Sarcomas,
Leukaemia, Osteosarcomas, Brain tumours and Adrenocortical carcinomas.
